rv.q: Najib has a knack for drawing you into her world, even if she pulls her punches in it.
But, directed by Jess Barton, the one-hour play lacks propulsion.

Societal observations abound throughout the piece and the trio under the direction of Jess Barton have honed delivery of some blinding one liners as they incorporate gently realised characterisations of the plethora of flat dwellers, visiting council inspectors and others impacted by events.

cn.t: Farah Najib's debut drama earns praise for its surprisingly engaging exploration of community responsibility and isolation, with critics commending the trio of storytellers who deliver this bleak yet compelling cautionary tale.
